questions.q: An IS auditor is planning the annual audit schedule. What should drive which areas receive the most audit attention?
choices: A risk-based assessment ranking auditable units by risk
The alphabetical order of business units
Requests received from individual department managers
The areas that were not audited in the prior year
questions.why: A risk-based approach directs limited audit resources to the highest-risk areas, which is the accepted basis for audit planning.

questions.q: During fieldwork an auditor gathers several types of evidence. Which is generally considered the most reliable?
choices: Evidence obtained directly by the auditor through observation and reperformance
Management's written representation letter
A copy of a report produced by the auditee
A verbal assurance from the process owner
questions.why: Evidence the auditor obtains directly is more reliable than evidence supplied by the auditee, because independence from the source reduces bias.

questions.q: An IS auditor wants each sampled item to have an equal and known chance of selection. Which sampling method achieves this?
choices: Judgmental sampling
Statistical sampling
Block sampling
Haphazard sampling
questions.why: Statistical sampling gives every item a known, non-zero probability of selection, allowing results to be projected to the population objectively.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of establishing materiality when planning an IS audit?
choices: To decide which staff auditors are assigned to the engagement
To calculate the audit fee charged to the client
To set the retention period for audit working papers
To determine the significance of findings and the extent of testing required
questions.why: Materiality helps the auditor judge whether an error or weakness is significant enough to affect decisions, guiding testing depth and reporting.

questions.q: An auditor's brother is the manager of the department scheduled for review. What is the appropriate action to preserve audit independence?
choices: Continue the audit since family relationships do not affect objectivity
Reduce the scope so only low-risk areas are tested
Proceed but have the brother review the final report
Disclose the relationship and reassign the auditor to a different engagement
questions.why: A close family relationship impairs independence in appearance and fact; disclosure and reassignment protect the objectivity of the engagement.

questions.q: An IS auditor identifies a control weakness during a walkthrough. What should be done before reporting it as a finding?
choices: Immediately escalate it to the audit committee
Corroborate the weakness with sufficient and appropriate evidence
Recommend that the process owner be terminated
Remove the control from the audit scope
questions.why: Findings must be supported by sufficient appropriate evidence before reporting; a single walkthrough observation should be corroborated.

questions.q: The risk that an IS auditor's substantive procedures fail to detect a material error is known as what?
choices: Business risk
Control risk
Detection risk
Inherent risk
questions.why: Detection risk is the risk that the auditor's own procedures will not catch a material misstatement that exists; it is the component the auditor directly controls.

questions.q: An auditor is deciding whether to rely on an automated application control. What should be verified FIRST?
choices: That the application has a modern user interface
That the relevant IT general controls over the application are effective
That the application vendor is financially stable
That end users are satisfied with the application
questions.why: Automated application controls can only be relied upon if the surrounding IT general controls, such as change and access management, are working.

questions.q: What is the MOST important reason for an IS auditor to prepare and retain working papers?
choices: To support the audit conclusions and provide evidence of work performed
To satisfy the curiosity of the auditee's staff
To replace the need for a formal audit report
To serve as a marketing document for future engagements
questions.why: Working papers document the evidence, analysis, and reasoning that support the auditor's conclusions and allow the work to be reviewed.

questions.q: An auditee disagrees with a reported finding. How should the IS auditor handle the disagreement in the final report?
choices: Report only findings that management accepts
Change the finding to match management's opinion
Remove the finding to avoid conflict
Include management's response alongside the finding without altering the facts
questions.why: The auditor reports facts objectively and includes management's response, but does not suppress or alter valid findings to gain agreement.

questions.q: A continuous auditing approach is being considered. What is its PRIMARY benefit compared to a traditional annual audit?
choices: It eliminates the need for any manual controls
It removes the requirement for management oversight
Control exceptions are identified closer to the time they occur
It reduces the qualifications required of the audit staff
questions.why: Continuous auditing detects anomalies in near real time, shortening the window between an exception occurring and its identification.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY objective of an IT governance framework such as COBIT?
choices: To replace the organization's financial accounting system
To align IT investments and activities with business objectives
To provide detailed programming standards for developers
To define the physical wiring of the data center
questions.why: IT governance frameworks ensure IT supports and enables enterprise objectives, delivering value while managing risk and resources.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews the IT steering committee. What is its MAIN responsibility?
choices: Performing daily system backups
Conducting penetration tests of the network
Prioritizing and approving major IT investments in line with strategy
Writing the source code for new applications
questions.why: The steering committee provides direction and prioritization for IT initiatives, ensuring investments align with business strategy and are properly resourced.

questions.q: When auditing IT strategy, what is the BEST indicator that IT is aligned with the business?
choices: IT staff hold the most industry certifications
The IT department has the newest available hardware
The CIO reports the largest budget in the organization
The IT strategic plan is derived from and supports the business strategy
questions.why: Alignment is demonstrated when the IT plan traces directly to business goals, ensuring technology investment supports enterprise priorities.

questions.q: An organization outsources its data center. Which responsibility can NOT be transferred to the service provider?
choices: Execution of routine backups
Accountability for the risk and control environment
Day-to-day operation of the servers
Physical maintenance of hardware
questions.why: Operations can be outsourced, but ultimate accountability for risk and controls remains with the organization's management.

questions.q: What should an IS auditor examine to assess whether IT risk is being managed at the enterprise level?
choices: The seating arrangement of the IT staff
A risk register linked to risk owners, ratings, and treatment plans
The brand of antivirus software installed
The number of help desk tickets closed each month
questions.why: A maintained risk register showing ownership, assessment, and treatment demonstrates a structured, accountable risk management process.

questions.q: An IS auditor finds that IT policies exist but have not been reviewed in five years. What is the PRIMARY concern?
choices: Policies may no longer reflect current risks, technology, or regulations
Employees have memorized the old policies
The policies are printed on outdated letterhead
The policies are too short to be useful
questions.why: Policies must be reviewed periodically so they stay relevant to evolving threats, technologies, and legal requirements.

questions.q: Segregation of duties is a key governance control. In an IT department, which combination represents an inappropriate lack of segregation?
choices: A developer who can also move their own code into production
An operator who runs jobs and a separate DBA who tunes the database
A developer who writes code and a separate team that tests it
A help desk agent who resets passwords after identity verification
questions.why: Allowing a developer to promote their own code to production removes an independent check and enables unauthorized or untested changes.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a service level agreement (SLA) with an IT vendor?
choices: To transfer legal accountability for compliance to the vendor
To grant the vendor ownership of the organization's data
To define measurable performance expectations and responsibilities
To eliminate the organization's need to monitor the vendor
questions.why: An SLA establishes agreed, measurable service levels and responsibilities so performance can be monitored and enforced.

questions.q: An IS auditor evaluates enterprise architecture. What is its PRIMARY governance value?
choices: It specifies the exact salary of each IT employee
It provides a blueprint linking business processes to supporting technology
It documents only the physical network cabling
It replaces the organization's project management office
questions.why: Enterprise architecture maps how business functions and IT components fit together, guiding consistent, aligned technology decisions.

questions.q: During a governance review, an auditor notes that IT performance is not measured. What should be recommended?
choices: Outsource all IT functions immediately
Increase the IT budget without any measurement
Establish key performance indicators tied to business objectives
Stop reporting to the board entirely
questions.why: Defined KPIs linked to objectives allow IT performance to be measured, monitored, and improved against business needs.

questions.q: Which document defines how an organization will respond to and recover from a disruptive incident affecting the whole business?
choices: Software licensing agreement
Business continuity plan
Data classification standard
Acceptable use policy
questions.why: The business continuity plan sets out how critical operations continue and recover after a disruption; it is broader than an IT-only recovery plan.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews a systems development project. When is it MOST cost-effective to correct a defect?
choices: During the requirements and design phases
During post-implementation review
After users report the defect in operations
After the system is deployed to production
questions.why: Defects are cheapest to fix early; the cost of correction rises sharply as the project moves toward and past implementation.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of user acceptance testing (UAT) before a system goes live?
choices: To verify that the source code compiles without errors
To test the physical security of the server room
To confirm the system meets business requirements from the user perspective
To measure the salary impact of the new system
questions.why: UAT validates that the delivered system satisfies the agreed business requirements, giving users a basis to accept it.

questions.q: An IS auditor is reviewing change management. What is the BEST evidence that a production change was authorized?
choices: An email thread discussing the change idea
The presence of the change in the production environment
An approved change request traceable to the implemented change
A verbal confirmation from the programmer
questions.why: A documented, approved change request linked to the actual change provides an audit trail proving proper authorization.

questions.q: Which application control ensures that data entered falls within a predefined acceptable range?
choices: A hash total on a backup file
A batch total reconciliation
A range or limit check
A parity check on the network
questions.why: A range or limit check is an input validation control that rejects values outside acceptable boundaries, preventing erroneous data entry.

questions.q: During acquisition of a software package, what should an IS auditor confirm regarding the vendor selection?
choices: Selection was based on documented requirements and objective criteria
The vendor is located nearest to the head office
The decision was made solely by the IT help desk
The vendor offered the most expensive product available
questions.why: A sound acquisition uses documented requirements and objective evaluation criteria so the chosen package best fits business needs.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY risk of migrating data to a new system without adequate reconciliation controls?
choices: Users will need less training on the new system
Data may be lost, duplicated, or corrupted during conversion
The old system cannot be decommissioned early
The new system will run faster than expected
questions.why: Without reconciliation between source and target, converted data may be incomplete or altered, undermining the integrity of the new system.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews program change controls and finds developers have direct write access to production libraries. What is the PRIMARY concern?
choices: Developers may work longer hours than necessary
The production library will consume more disk space
Unauthorized or untested code could be introduced into production
Documentation will become too detailed
questions.why: Developer write access to production bypasses change controls and segregation of duties, allowing unapproved or untested changes to go live.

questions.q: What is the MAIN purpose of a post-implementation review after a system goes live?
choices: To retrain the entire IT department
To assess whether the project met its objectives and delivered expected benefits
To immediately begin building a replacement system
To assign blame for any defects found
questions.why: A post-implementation review evaluates whether the delivered system achieved its objectives and expected benefits and captures lessons learned.

questions.q: An organization uses agile development. What should an IS auditor verify about controls in this environment?
choices: Key controls such as approvals and testing are embedded in each iteration
That developers self-approve all their own changes
That controls are only applied to the final release years later
That no documentation of any kind is produced
questions.why: Agile still requires controls; the auditor confirms that approvals, testing, and reviews are built into iterative delivery rather than skipped.

questions.q: Which control best detects that a batch of transactions was processed completely and without loss?
choices: A firewall rule review
A biometric access log
An antivirus signature update
Reconciliation of run-to-run control totals
questions.why: Run-to-run control totals compare record counts and amounts across processing stages to confirm completeness and detect lost transactions.

questions.q: When auditing a project's business case, what should the IS auditor primarily evaluate?
choices: Whether expected benefits, costs, and risks justify the investment
Whether the project sponsor has a corner office
Whether the newest programming language was chosen
Whether the project team prefers remote work
questions.why: A business case should demonstrate that projected benefits outweigh costs and risks, justifying the use of organizational resources.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews the recovery point objective (RPO) for a critical system. What does the RPO define?
choices: The maximum time allowed to restore the system
The maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time
The number of staff required in the recovery team
The physical distance to the backup site
questions.why: The RPO specifies how much data, expressed as a time interval, the organization can afford to lose, driving backup frequency.

questions.q: The recovery time objective (RTO) for a payroll system is four hours. What does this mean?
choices: The system may lose up to four hours of data
The system must be restored to operation within four hours of disruption
Backups must be taken every four hours
The recovery team must arrive within four hours
questions.why: The RTO is the target duration within which a business process or system must be restored after an outage to avoid unacceptable impact.

questions.q: Which type of disaster recovery site can be operational in the shortest time?
choices: A cold site with only space and utilities
A warm site with hardware but no current data
A hot site with equipment and current data ready
A reciprocal agreement with another company
questions.why: A hot site is fully equipped and kept current, so it can take over operations quickly, giving the shortest recovery time.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews backup procedures. What is the MOST important test of backup effectiveness?
choices: Periodic restoration tests confirming data can be recovered
Confirming the backup software has a modern interface
Verifying the color coding of the tape labels
Counting how many backup tapes are stored
questions.why: Backups are only useful if they can be restored; regular restoration testing is the definitive evidence of backup effectiveness.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a business impact analysis (BIA) in continuity planning?
choices: To select the vendor for new servers
To determine employee vacation schedules
To design the corporate logo
To identify critical processes and the impact of their disruption over time
questions.why: The BIA identifies critical processes and quantifies the impact of disruption, providing the basis for recovery priorities and objectives.

questions.q: An IS auditor observes that the DR plan has never been tested. What is the PRIMARY risk?
choices: The plan document will take up storage space
Staff will read the plan too frequently
The plan may fail to work as intended during an actual disaster
The plan will become popular with auditors
questions.why: An untested plan may contain gaps or outdated assumptions that only surface during a real event, when it is too late to fix them.

questions.q: Which incident management activity should occur FIRST when a major system outage is detected?
choices: Identify and classify the incident by severity and impact
Archive the incident for future training
Award the response team a bonus
Write the final root cause report
questions.why: Detecting, identifying, and classifying the incident by severity comes first so the appropriate response and resources can be mobilized.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews capacity management. What is its PRIMARY objective?
choices: To increase the number of servers regardless of need
To reduce the number of IT staff
To slow down system performance intentionally
To ensure IT resources meet current and future demand efficiently
questions.why: Capacity management ensures resources are sufficient to meet demand cost-effectively, avoiding both shortages and wasteful over-provisioning.

questions.q: When reviewing IT operations, what is the BEST control to detect unauthorized changes to production job schedules?
choices: Painting the data center walls
Increasing the office temperature
A monthly team lunch meeting
Review of scheduler logs against approved change records
questions.why: Comparing scheduler activity logs to approved changes detects any unauthorized modifications to production job schedules.

questions.q: An IS auditor evaluates offsite storage of backup media. What is the MOST important consideration?
choices: The offsite site has the same street name
The offsite staff wear matching uniforms
The offsite location is far enough to avoid the same disaster yet accessible
The offsite building has an attractive lobby
questions.why: Offsite storage must be far enough that a regional disaster does not destroy both copies, while remaining accessible for timely recovery.

questions.q: Which metric best measures the reliability of a critical production system for an operations audit?
choices: The number of stickers on the monitors
The age of the server chassis
System availability or uptime against agreed targets
The number of coffee breaks taken by operators
questions.why: Availability measured against agreed targets shows whether the system is reliably meeting operational and service commitments.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews access controls and applies the principle of least privilege. What does this principle require?
choices: Users choose their own access levels
Users are granted only the access needed to perform their duties
Access is granted permanently and never reviewed
All users receive administrator rights for convenience
questions.why: Least privilege limits each user to the minimum access necessary for their role, reducing the risk of misuse and error.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a periodic user access review?
choices: To confirm access rights remain appropriate for current job responsibilities
To reset the network switches
To upgrade the email client for all users
To increase the total number of user accounts
questions.why: Access reviews detect excessive, stale, or orphaned rights so that privileges continue to match users' current responsibilities.

questions.q: An IS auditor examines data classification. What is its PRIMARY benefit for protecting information assets?
choices: It makes all data publicly available
It encrypts only the least sensitive data
It ensures controls are applied commensurate with data sensitivity
It deletes data that is rarely used
questions.why: Classification lets the organization apply protection proportional to sensitivity, avoiding both under-protection and wasteful over-protection.

questions.q: Which control provides accountability by ensuring actions can be traced to a specific individual?
choices: Unique user IDs combined with logging
A single password posted at each desk
Anonymous guest access
Shared generic accounts for the whole team
questions.why: Unique IDs plus activity logging tie actions to individuals, establishing accountability; shared accounts destroy traceability.

questions.q: During a review of privileged accounts, what is the BEST practice an IS auditor should expect to find?
choices: Privileged activity is logged and independently monitored
Privileged access is granted without approval
All staff share one administrator password
Administrators disable logging to improve speed
questions.why: Because privileged accounts carry high risk, their activity should be logged and independently monitored to detect misuse.

questions.q: An IS auditor assesses physical access to the data center. Which control best restricts entry to authorized personnel?
choices: Badge access with logging and an entry authorization list
A decorative gate that is always open
A suggestion box near the door
A sign asking visitors to be quiet
questions.why: Badge-controlled entry with logging enforces and records who is authorized to enter the data center, deterring and detecting unauthorized access.

questions.q: What is the PRIMARY security concern when an employee is terminated?
choices: Updating the company phone directory design
Scheduling a farewell lunch
Recovering the employee's office chair
Timely revocation of all logical and physical access
questions.why: Prompt removal of access on termination prevents a former employee from retaining the ability to access systems or facilities.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews multi-factor authentication. Which combination represents true multi-factor authentication?
choices: Two different passwords entered in sequence
A password plus a one-time code from a hardware token
A password plus a security question
A username plus a password
questions.why: MFA requires factors from different categories; a password (something you know) plus a token (something you have) qualifies, while two passwords do not.

questions.q: An IS auditor evaluates a firewall rule set. What is the BEST configuration principle to verify?
choices: Rules chosen at random each week
Default deny, permitting only explicitly authorized traffic
Default allow, blocking only known bad traffic
All ports open for maximum flexibility
questions.why: A default-deny stance permits only explicitly required traffic, minimizing the attack surface compared with a default-allow approach.

questions.q: When auditing log management, what is the MOST important control to preserve the integrity of audit logs?
choices: Allowing every user to edit the logs freely
Storing logs on a protected system where administrators cannot alter them
Deleting logs daily to save space
Printing logs and discarding the originals
questions.why: Logs must be protected from tampering, ideally on a separate system, so administrators cannot alter records of their own actions.

questions.q: An IS auditor reviews handling of personally identifiable information (PII). What is the PRIMARY control objective?
choices: Ensuring PII is collected, used, and retained per privacy requirements
Retaining PII indefinitely regardless of need
Sharing PII with any requesting party
Publishing all PII on the public website
questions.why: Protecting PII means limiting collection, use, and retention to what is lawful and necessary under applicable privacy requirements.
